Run differential expression analysis on a single study

Source: R/03_de.R
mx_de.Rd

Performs differential expression analysis on one metaXpressStudy using DESeq2, edgeR (quasi-likelihood), or limma-voom. Stores the full result (all tested genes) in the de_result slot of the returned study object, in a common format that mx_meta consumes directly.

Usage

mx_de(
  study,
  method = c("DESeq2", "edgeR", "limma-voom"),
  formula = ~condition,
  contrast = NULL,
  shrink = c("none", "apeglm", "ashr", "normal"),
  ...
)

Arguments

study

A metaXpressStudy object with raw counts.

method

Character scalar. DE method. One of "DESeq2" (default), "edgeR", or "limma-voom".

formula

A design formula whose variables are columns of colData(study). Must contain condition; any other terms (e.g. ~ sex + age + condition) are adjusted for. Default: ~ condition.

contrast

Optional length-2 character vector c(case_level, control_level) naming the two condition levels to compare. Fold changes are case / control. When NULL, the control level is auto-detected (e.g. "control", "normal", "healthy", "untreated") and the first other level is the case. Set this explicitly for every study in a meta-analysis so fold-change directions agree.

shrink

Character scalar. Optional log fold-change shrinkage for DESeq2: "none" (default), "apeglm", "ashr" or "normal". Shrunken values are added as log2FC_shrunk for ranking and plotting; the unshrunken maximum-likelihood log2FC and lfcSE are always kept because inverse-variance meta-analysis requires unbiased estimates with their sampling variance.

...

Additional arguments passed to DESeq2::DESeq(), edgeR::glmQLFit() or limma::lmFit().

Value

The input study with the de_result slot populated. de_result is a data.frame with columns:

gene_id

Gene identifier (rownames of the count matrix).

log2FC

Log2 fold change, case vs control.

lfcSE

Standard error of log2FC (log2 scale).

stat

Signed standard-normal test statistic (sign(log2FC) * qnorm(pvalue / 2, lower.tail = FALSE) for edgeR/limma, the Wald statistic for DESeq2).

pvalue, padj

Raw and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values.

baseMean

Mean normalized expression.

n_case, n_control

Number of samples in each group, used by mx_meta for sample-size weighting.

method

DE engine used.

The case and control labels are stored in attr(de_result, "contrast").

Details

For edgeR and limma-voom, low-count genes are removed with edgeR::filterByExpr() before testing; DESeq2 applies its own independent filtering to padj but reports all genes. Genes removed by filtering are treated as not measured in that study and are handled explicitly by Module 5 (mx_missing_summary).

For edgeR, standard errors are back-calculated from the quasi-likelihood test as |log2FC| / |z|, where z is the normal quantile of the two-sided p-value. This places all three engines on the same log2-scale effect/variance footing required for inverse-variance meta-analysis (Rau et al. 2014).

Use padj (not raw pvalue) for per-study significance calls.

References

Love, M.I., Huber, W. & Anders, S. (2014) Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2. Genome Biology, 15(12), 550. doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8

Chen, Y., Lun, A.T.L. & Smyth, G.K. (2016) From reads to genes to pathways: differential expression analysis of RNA-Seq experiments using Rsubread and the edgeR quasi-likelihood pipeline. F1000Research, 5, 1438. doi:10.12688/f1000research.8987.2

Law, C.W. et al. (2014) voom: precision weights unlock linear model analysis tools for RNA-seq read counts. Genome Biology, 15(2), R29. doi:10.1186/gb-2014-15-2-r29

Zhu, A., Ibrahim, J.G. & Love, M.I. (2019) Heavy-tailed prior distributions for sequence count data: removing the noise and preserving large differences. Bioinformatics, 35(12), 2084–2092. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty895

See also

mx_de_all, mx_de_summary, mx_meta

Examples

if (requireNamespace("airway", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("DESeq2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # Himes et al. (2014) airway smooth muscle cells, GEO GSE52778:
  # dexamethasone vs untreated, paired by donor cell line.
  data("airway", package = "airway")
  study <- mx_from_se(airway, condition_col = "dex",
                      accession = "GSE52778")
  study <- study[rowSums(SummarizedExperiment::assay(study)) >= 10, ]
  study <- mx_de(study, formula = ~ cell + condition,
                 contrast = c("trt", "untrt"))
  de <- study@de_result
  head(de[order(de$padj), ])
}
